clue.text: Railway enthusiast coaches a worker in ceramics

explanation.surface: A rail fan apparently tutors someone who works in a pottery.

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who collects locomotive numbers as a hobby is the classic British railway hobbyist.

clue.text: Paddy has so much French spirit

explanation.surface: An Irishman named Paddy drinks a lot of French liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like a name, but in British English a paddy is a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy is British slang for a fit of bad temper, the same thing as a childish outburst.

clue.text: Very little seafood is put in a herbal garnish

explanation.definitionFit: A tiny sea plant is a very small thing that grows in the sea, so loosely a minimal sea food.

clue.text: Unjust way to describe a brunette

explanation.surface: Calling a dark-haired woman something is unfair to her.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unjust is inequitable; a brunette has dark hair, so she is the opposite of blonde, or light-haired.

is shortened to 's, as in it's

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'cannabis is stolen' as POT'S HOT.

clue.text: Go for a spin

explanation.surface: Take the car out for a drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A go is one's opportunity or move in a game; a spin is a rotation or twirl.

clue.text: The food of rasher Elizabethan and Georgian statesmen?

explanation.surface: A question about what Tudor and Georgian politicians ate.
explanation.walkthrough: The 4th Earl of Sandwich is said to have invented the snack by eating meat between slices of bread at the gaming table.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasher is a slice of bacon, and a snack made with rashers between bread is a classic British meal.

clue.text: The time to take that gin cocktail?

clue.text: A dour Scot is hiding yours and mine

clue.text: Tree most appropriate for the kirk

explanation.surface: A tree that would suit a Scottish church best.
explanation.walkthrough: A kirk is a Scottish church, whose lay officers carry this title.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small tree with white flowers and dark berries; in Presbyterian churches it is also a senior lay office-holder.

clue.text: He tempts many to sin

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
evil is wickedness or sin

explanation.surface: A tempter leading lots of people astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan is the great tempter in Christian tradition, luring people into wrongdoing.

clue.text: One who tries to make a piece of embroidery

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tastes or tests things tries them; it is also a stitched cloth showing letters and patterns.

clue.text: Operations room is where the drama is

explanation.surface: A hospital room where all the excitement happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery takes place in an operating suite; plays are staged in a playhouse.

clue.text: Did President Roosevelt's policy call for a reshuffle?

explanation.surface: Asking whether an American President's programme demanded a cabinet change.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a card player asking for the cards to be dealt again.
explanation.definitionFit: FDR's 1930s recovery programme had this name; at cards it asks for a fresh hand.

clue.text: Charming encouragement not to lose them all

definitions.text: encouragement not to lose them all

explanation.surface: A pleasant reminder that you will not always be beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the saying 'you win some, you lose some'.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming means appealing and engaging; the second reading cheers a loser up.

clue.text: The young bounder always gets let outside

explanation.walkthrough: 'bounder' looks like a cad, but here it is a hare, which bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A hare in its first year is called by this name, and hares bound along.

clue.text: He may get a bird's-eye view of a Roman road and hill

a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

clue.text: Contract to construct a flyover

clue.text: Lack desire

clue.text: Despite that, is it for evermore?
